summary: Tested v5 TRANSFER + per-warehouse ADJUST/REMOVE + PDF Needs-Reordering features. Backend: created /app/backend/tests/test_transfers_v5.py with 12 new pytest cases covering (a) /api/transfers happy path keeps total + writes both stock keys, (b) same-warehouse rejected 400, (c) insufficient stock rejected 400 with no state mutation, (d) negative qty rejected 400, (e) transfer movement is recorded with from_warehouse_id+resulting_qty+resulting_total, (f) adjust sets only target warehouse and recomputes total, (g) remove subtracts only target and floors at 0, (h) remove on non-target warehouse leaves others intact, (i) per-warehouse low_stock flag (w1=200 not low, w2=2 low), (j) reorder-suggestions returns suggested_qty=max(threshold,2*threshold-qty), (k) dashboard no-filter lists per-(product,warehouse) low rows, (l) dashboard ?warehouse_id scopes totals. RESULT: 12/12 NEW PASS. Full regression: 59/59 PASS (previous v4 legacy regression fixed — test_product_lifecycle_with_movement and test_snapshot_updated_by_movement now green). Frontend Playwright (390x844): logged in as warehouse@test.com, navigated to /product/<id> for a product seeded with 20@Main + 8@Gothenburg. Verified: (i) all three FABs render (quick-receive-btn, adjust-btn, transfer-btn — testIDs present), (ii) Adjust modal opens with warehouse picker showing 'Main Warehouse 20' + 'Gothenburg DC 8' chips and Set-to/Remove buttons; Set-to 13 succeeded (modal closed); Remove 3 succeeded (Main now shows 10), (iii) Transfer modal opens with FROM + TO pickers — TO list correctly excludes the selected FROM warehouse; empty qty triggers 'Enter a quantity' validation; over-transfer qty (999999) triggers 'Not enough stock' validation; valid transfer (2 units Main→Gothenburg) succeeded and modal closed, (iv) Orders tab renders export-csv-btn, export-pdf-btn, filter-wh-all + per-warehouse filter chips. PDF Needs-Reordering section was code-reviewed in orders.tsx:102-111 (Print.printToFileAsync HTML emits 'Needs Reordering (N)' table with warehouse|product|supplier|qty|threshold|suggestedOrder columns when any row.warehouse && row.quantity <= row.threshold; sorted by warehouse+name; honors filterWh/filterCat because buildRows() applies both filters). No red-screen errors. Cosmetic warning carries over: 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated' on react-native-web Pressable.

minor.issue: Still returns 200 silently when matched_count==0 (carryover from prior iterations).

Does not validate that from_warehouse_id or to_warehouse_id exist as real warehouses owned by the user. Currently any string passes if it's not == the other and source qty is 0/sufficient. Suggest validating both ids against db.warehouses before mutation.
Does not validate that warehouse_id in payload actually exists/owned by user — silently creates a new key in product.stock for an unknown wid. Same pattern.
Pre-existing benign 'module bcrypt has no attribute __about__' passlib warning.

issues: Three stacked FABs (Receive/Adjust/Transfer) sit at right-bottom (+84, +140, +196). On taller screens fine; on small phones (<700pt) they can overlap the Save Changes button at bottom. Consider grouping into a single 'Actions' menu or a horizontally-arranged action bar.

The 'To' chip row shows every other warehouse including ones with 0 stock — fine, but if user has many warehouses (current test account has 44 because of test-fixture pollution) the horizontal scroll becomes long. Consider showing wh-name only without the trailing qty for the 'To' picker.

react_native_issues.issue: Carryover: 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents' warning. Cosmetic only — fix when convenient by moving pointerEvents into the style object on the offending Pressable/View.

action_items: (Low) Validate warehouse_id existence/ownership on POST /api/transfers and POST /api/movements so unknown ids return 404 instead of silently mutating product.stock.
(Low / carryover) Return 404 from PUT /api/warehouses|categories|suppliers when matched_count==0.
(Low / carryover) Silence the react-native-web pointerEvents deprecation warning.

(Hygiene) Clean up TEST_-prefixed warehouses left over from previous test runs (44 currently in db for warehouse@test.com) so the catalog/transfer-modal chip rows stay short — or have tests delete their warehouses in teardown (currently only products and explicit fixtures are cleaned).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:451-479 transfer_stock — does not validate that body.from_warehouse_id or body.to_warehouse_id correspond to an actual warehouse owned by the user. Insufficient-stock check guards source, but the destination key is created with int(stock.get(to_wid,0))+qty regardless, so a typo'd to_warehouse_id will silently create an orphan stock entry that nothing in the UI surfaces.

server.py:397-433 create_movement — same blind-trust of body.warehouse_id (no existence check). Should reject with 404 'Warehouse not found' when wid is non-null and not in db.warehouses for the user.

orders.tsx:102 — reorder filter uses `r.warehouse && r.quantity <= r.threshold` which drops the synthesised empty-warehouse row from buildRows(). Good — unstocked products won't appear in the Needs Reordering section even if their product-level qty<threshold.
orders.tsx:105 suggestedOrder = Math.max(r.threshold, r.threshold*2 - r.quantity) — matches backend reorder_suggestions math (max(threshold, threshold*2-qty)). Consistent.

product/[id].tsx:54-59 doReceive — passes activeWh (which can be a saved warehouse from AsyncStorage that no longer exists if the user deleted it). Combined with the backend's lack of warehouse existence validation (see above), this could create dangling stock entries.

product/[id].tsx:68-74 openTransfer auto-picks the first non-zero source AND a non-source destination — good UX. But if the product has stock in only one warehouse, To picker can be null and validation catches it (pickTwoWarehouses). Verified.
server.py is now 784 lines (was 742 in v4) — still past the 700-line module-split threshold. Recommend extracting models, auth, products, movements, reports into separate routers.

Pollution risk: pytest fixtures in test_transfers_v5.py and test_per_warehouse_stock.py do NOT delete the warehouses they create — only products. Each pytest run adds ~10 TEST_ warehouses to the shared warehouse@test.com user. After multiple iterations this account now has 44 warehouses. Recommend a session-level autouse fixture that purges TEST_-prefixed warehouses.
